content: 1. A systematic review was conducted to evaluate adherence to oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV and to identify strategies to improve both uptake and adherence. This study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2018 (Volume 18, Article 581). 2. Landovitz RJ and colleagues investigated the use of cabotegravir for HIV prevention in cisgender men and transgender women. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2021 (Volume 385, Pages 595-608). 3. Delany-Moretlwe S and colleagues reported on the efficacy of cabotegravir for HIV-1 prevention in women, based on results from the HPTN 084 Phase 3 randomized clinical trial. This study was published in The Lancet in 2022 (Volume 399, Pages 1779-1789). 4. Landovitz RJ and colleagues demonstrated that cabotegravir was not associated with weight gain in HIV-uninfected individuals participating in the HPTN 077 study. This research was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2020 (Volume 70, Pages 319-322). 5. Marzinke MA and colleagues characterized HIV infections in cisgender men and transgender women who have sex with men and were receiving injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention as part of the HPTN 083 study. Their findings were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2021 (Volume 224, Pages 1581-1592). 6. Eshleman SH and colleagues analyzed HIV infections in women who received either injectable cabotegravir or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine for HIV prevention in the HPTN 084 study. This work was submitted to the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2022. 7. Delany-Moretlwe S and colleagues evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics of long-acting cabotegravir (CAB-LA) in pregnant women during the blinded phase of the HPTN 084 study. These findings were presented at the 2022 Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI). 8. Glaubius RL and colleagues assessed the cost-effectiveness of injectable PrEP for HIV prevention in South Africa. Their study was published in Reviews of Infectious Diseases in 2016 (Volume 63, Pages 539-547). 9. Quaife M and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness of multi-purpose technologies for HIV and pregnancy prevention in South Africa. This research was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2018 (Volume 21, Article e25064). 10. Smith JA, Garnett GP, and Hallett TB conducted a mathematical modeling study to assess the potential impact of long-acting cabotegravir for HIV prevention in South Africa. Their findings were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2021 (Volume 224, Pages 1179-1186). 11. Van Vliet MM and colleagues modeled the epidemiological impact and cost-effectiveness of providing long-acting PrEP to injectable contraceptive users for HIV prevention in South Africa. This study was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019 (Volume 22, Article e25427). 12. Vogelzang M and colleagues analyzed the cost-effectiveness of HIV PrEP among heterosexual men in South Africa using a cost-utility modeling approach. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes (JAIDS) in 2020 (Volume 84, Pages 173-181). 13. Walensky RP and colleagues explored the clinical and economic value of long-acting PrEP for South African women at high risk for HIV infection. This study was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2016 (Volume 213, Pages 1523-1531). 14. Neilan AM and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness of long-acting injectable HIV PrEP in the United States. Their findings were published in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2022. 15. Bahati Ngongo P and colleagues conducted a survey of stakeholder perceptions regarding PrEP, prospective HIV microbicides, and vaccines in Kenya. This study was published in AIDS Clinical Research in 2017 (Volume 8, Article 1000678). 16. Xavier Hall CD and colleagues explored healthcare providers' perspectives on preparing for long-acting injectable PrEP in the Southern United States, specifically in Georgia. Their findings were published in AIDS Care in 2021 (Volume 33, Pages 706-711). 17. Hershow RB and colleagues examined medical providers' and harm reduction specialists' views on PrEP for HIV prevention among people who inject drugs. This study was published in AIDS Education and Prevention in 2019 (Volume 31, Pages 363-379).
